params.body:
Live trends get what people posted, not only what reports said.

On 2 October 21 of the 61 trends on gentells.com rested on fewer than five platform observations, four on none, while the corpus held 234,000 signals. Patterns are built with a report weighing double a sighting, so the posts never reached the trend.

- **`packages/core/signal-search.mjs`**: SQLite FTS5 over `raw_content` and `notes` (the classifier's English note, so a Chinese hot-list entry is found in English), external content, kept current by triggers, built on first use (7.5 s on a copy of production; a search takes 0.1 to 0.2 s). `searchSignals` filters to observed platforms in the query and requires at least two of the trend's words in a candidate.
- **`packages/pipeline/widen-evidence.mjs`**: per live trend, search with the words of its headline and reading, let Opus 5.5 (the deepen role) judge which candidates are an instance of the trend, with a one-sentence reason for each, and fold the confirmed ones in with `foldInto` (strength recomputed). A signal backs one trend; posts about self-harm or suicide are left out before any model sees them. Dry by default (`store/widen-dry.json`), `--apply`, `--apply --from <reviewed.json>` to fold exactly what was reviewed, `--undo <ids>`; every write keeps the previous signal list in `widen_undo`.
- Haiku first, on a copy: 145 signals for 43 trends, too lenient (a gaming stream as "creators open about brand deals"). Opus 5.5 with reasons: 75 for 30, 73 after the sensitive filter.

`test/signal-search.test.mjs`. Not scheduled yet: it runs by hand until its yield and cost have been watched.
params.title: Evidence: own observations for live trends
